label: AQ 0004
title: The edit that missed its line

questions.q: SWE-agent's edit command uses line numbers. Why did it work?
questions.a: Its file viewer printed fresh line numbers next to the code and showed the file again after each edit, so the numbers were never stale. Line numbers fail when they're out of date or the model has to work them out.

teach.title: How it works: an edit tool built for a model

questions.a: No. Aider found GPT-4 Turbo did better with a simplified diff than with its search/replace blocks (61% vs 20% on 89 refactoring tasks), but that diff had its line numbers dropped, and each change was applied by matching its content. The lesson is “anchor on content”, whatever the format.

questions.q: What if the old text appears twice?
questions.a: The tool refuses and asks for a few more surrounding lines to make the match unique. Guessing would edit the wrong place silently.

questions.q: Why do line numbers in a second edit go wrong?
questions.a: The first edit added or removed lines, so everything below it moved. The old numbers now point at different code.

questions.q: What should a content-anchored edit do if the old text matches nowhere, or in two places?
questions.a: Change nothing and return a clear error: “not found”, or “several matches, add more context”.

questions.q: In SWE-agent's test, what happened without a proper edit command?
questions.a: The agent fixed 10.3% of SWE-bench Lite instead of 18.0%, with the same model.
